reports.title: Zoetis Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results; Highlights Progress Advancing Innovation Across Diversified Portfolio and Narrows Full Year 2026 Revenue Guidance, Raises Full Year 2026 Adjusted EPS Guidance

guidance.heading: FULL YEAR 2026 FINANCIAL GUIDANCE
section: •Narrowed revenue to a range of $9.220 billion to $9.320 billion (organic operational growth of (2)% to (1)%)
•Raised adjusted net income to a range of $2.600 billion to $2.640 billion (organic operational growth of (7)% to (5)%)
•Raised adjusted diluted EPS to a range of $6.25 to $6.35

This guidance reflects foreign exchange rates as of October 20, 2026. Additional details on guidance, including reconciliations of non-GAAP financial measures and the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures, are included in the financial tables and will be discussed on the company's conference call.

desk.headline: Revenue down 1% to $2.39bn but EPS beat; full-year EPS guidance raised, revenue range narrowed
results: Revenue slipped 1% to $2.39bn; adjusted EPS rose 3% to $1.75, while GAAP EPS fell 12% to $1.44 after an $89m impairment and restructuring costs.
US sales fell 6%: pet medicine sales dropped 8% on price-sensitive owners, dermatology competition and generics; US livestock grew 5%.
International sales rose 4%, led by livestock (+8%), especially cattle and fish; international pet sales were flat on an organic basis.
Fewer shares outstanding (411.6m vs 443.2m diluted) helped EPS grow while adjusted net income fell 5% to $720m.
New approvals included Convenia RTU for dogs in the US, due to reach vets in Q1 2027.

guidance.summary: Zoetis raised its 2026 adjusted EPS range to $6.25–6.35 and adjusted net income to $2.60–2.64bn, and narrowed revenue to $9.22–9.32bn by lifting the bottom. GAAP EPS guidance edged down to $5.50–5.60 on higher one-off charges. No 2027 guidance yet.

points: Key dermatology sales fell 16% to $396m as Apoquel lost share, but the share loss slowed to about 4 points from about 7 in Q2.
US Librela sales were hurt by fewer arthritis vet visits and safety perceptions; US canine visits were down about 5%.
Management expects dermatology share to settle 12–18 months after rivals arrived and wants two stable quarters before chasing share gains.
The second half is expected to decline high single digits, with Q4 weaker than Q3; cost savings continue into 2027.
2027 planning will be cautious, assuming no macro relief or easing competition, with new launches mattering more in 2028.
